entries.ready: text=3 issues in flight, 12 queued behind them.
entries.caption: Mission Control — live loops, the queue, the build farm and what needs you, at a glance.
entries.alt: The Ouroboros Mission Control dashboard for the Acme Robotics workspace, showing active loops, the queue and farm status.

entries.caption: One loop in the run console: its stage timeline, the agent's transcript and the changes so far.
entries.alt: The run console for a loop fixing a flaky CAN-bus telemetry test: the stage timeline with three stages done and Implementing on attempt 2 of 3, the agent transcript, and three changed files.

entries.caption: The sign-in page: continue with GitHub or your company's single sign-on.
entries.alt: The Ouroboros sign-in page, with the brand panel on the left and, on the right, Step 1 Sign in with Continue with GitHub and an enterprise SSO domain field, and a Step 2 preview of choosing where the loop runs.

entries.caption: The detection card: what Ouroboros found in the repository, with the evidence for each finding.
entries.alt: The We already figured this out card, listing the repository's language, build, devcontainer, tests, suggested protected paths and conventions.

entries.caption: Starting workflow templates — pick one, then edit it later in the Workflow Studio.
entries.alt: The Choose a starting workflow card with four template tiles: Quick fixes, Feature builder, Docs & chores and Deep refactor.

entries.caption: Your first issue: the safe one Ouroboros picked, with its estimate, and what keeps the first loop safe.
entries.alt: The Your first issue card showing the picked issue with its effort, workflow and estimated minutes, the buttons to pick another, and the safety list.

entries.caption: Smart defaults: what is already set up for you, and what you can add later.
entries.alt: The Smart defaults card, listing models through your own keys, builds on an enrolled runner, the nightly estimator and Slack after your first pull request.

entries.caption: What keeps the first loop safe: dry-run opens a draft pull request and never merges.
entries.alt: The safety list under the first issue: dry-run opens a draft PR and never merges, decisions wait in the Needs-you inbox, and auto-merge can be turned on in Settings, Policies.

entries.caption: A new workspace's dashboard offers the Get Started wizard until you run a first loop or dismiss it.
entries.alt: The Mission Control dashboard of a new workspace, with a banner reading New workspace — your first loop in about 4 minutes, and Get started and Dismiss buttons.

entries.caption: The app shell: the sidebar on the left, the header across the top, and the screen you are on in between.
entries.alt: The Ouroboros app on the Mission Control dashboard: the sidebar listing Dashboard to Insights with Needs You and Settings at its foot, and the header with the workspace chip, Search, the live-loop and Needs you pills, the bell and the account avatar.

entries.caption: The search palette: type to find a screen or a command, then press Enter.
entries.alt: The search palette open, with the Search screens and commands field, the Navigation group of Go to commands and the Actions group with Toggle theme and Sign out.

entries.caption: The account menu: font size, theme, workspace settings, keyboard shortcuts and sign out.
entries.alt: The account menu open under the avatar, showing your name and email, the Font size stepper, the Theme choices Light, Dark and System, and the Workspace settings, Keyboard shortcuts and Sign out items.

entries.caption: Issue intake: every open issue, sized before you ask, with its suggested workflow and model.
entries.alt: The Issues screen for Acme Robotics headed 9 open issues, 7 already sized, with Re-estimate all and Queue 0 selected buttons, a filter bar of repository, label chips, state, sort and search, and the backlog table showing each issue's effort chip and confidence, suggested workflow and routed model, beside an empty Issue detail panel.

entries.caption: An issue's sizing story: the estimate, its confidence and regression risk, and how it was produced.
entries.alt: The Issue detail panel for #484 Motor PID integral windup on wheel stall, marked sized, with its description, the AI work breakdown listing two files, about 150k tokens, a 10–16 minute cycle time, effort M at 88% confidence, medium regression risk with its reason, the standard-fix workflow and cursor/composer-2 model, the Queue for loop, Re-estimate and Open on GitHub buttons, and the estimation trace.

entries.caption: Three issues ticked: the selection bar totals their estimate and queues them under a workflow.
entries.alt: The backlog with #484, #489 and #487 ticked and, along the bottom, the selection bar reading 3 issues selected, est. 3h 40m combined autonomous work, with an Assign workflow menu button and a Queue → suggested button.

entries.caption: Planning: describe the work and draft tickets, with the trackers and the backlog's health beside it.
entries.alt: The Planning screen headed Describe the work. Ouroboros writes the tickets., with Import from Jira marked soon and New roadmap buttons; the Generate tickets card with its description box, structured outline, tracker choice of GitHub Issues, Jira and Linear, milestone select, the Auto-size with estimator and Queue XS/S tickets immediately switches and the Draft tickets button; and the Tracker sync and Backlog health cards.

entries.caption: A drafted batch under review: six tickets, sized and wired with dependencies. Nothing reaches the tracker until you push.
entries.alt: The Draft — 6 tickets list marked all sized: six ticked drafts OTA-1 to OTA-6, each with its title, the tickets it blocks, an effort chip, a suggested workflow and an Edit button, above the estimated total, Regenerate and Push 6 tickets to GitHub.

entries.caption: The roadmap: one lane per epic across the months, with progress and today's date.
entries.alt: The Roadmap — Helios 2.1 card, Q3 2026 to Q1 2027, with Share marked soon: a month grid from July 2026 to March 2027 with bars for OTA hardening (12 issues, 8 done), BLE provisioning v2 (9, 2), Motor control refactor (14, 0), Fleet telemetry dashboard (7, 0) and a dashed unscoped Zephyr 4.2 migration marked proposed, a TODAY line, and an Add epic button.

entries.caption: The push: one press writes every ticked draft to the tracker, blockers first.
entries.alt: The foot of a drafted batch: est. total ~3 days of loop time · $14 est. spend, a Regenerate button and the Push 6 tickets to GitHub button.
